narrative.intro: Softrams has $217M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Softrams has 18 awards this year, with an average award size of $12M and obligations up 4.8% year over year. Softrams' obligations rose steadily from $70.2M in FY21 to $217M in FY26, with intermediate totals of $77.7M in FY22, $125M in FY23, $158M in FY24, and $207M in FY25. Softrams concentrates its FY2026 buying with the Department of Health and Human Services at $177M, followed by the Department of Veterans Affairs at $25.9M and the Department of Homeland Security at $13.4M. Softrams also records obligations with the General Services Administration at $279K; separate entries list the Department of Defense and the Department of Labor without dollar figures shown here. Softrams' work maps mostly to a few NAICS markets: Custom Computer Programming Services at $182M and Computer Systems Design Services at $34.8M. The balance of obligations and the award mix show a vendor focused on health-related IT and systems work in the current fiscal year.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Softrams' federal obligations?
sections.body: Softrams' obligations are concentrated in a few agencies and markets. The Department of Health and Human Services accounts for $177M of FY2026 obligations, and Custom Computer Programming Services accounts for $182M of FY2026 obligations. The top three agencies together include the Department of Veterans Affairs at $25.9M and the Department of Homeland Security at $13.4M. The remaining obligations are smaller, including $279K with the General Services Administration and entries for the Department of Defense and the Department of Labor without dollar figures shown here.

sections.heading: How has Softrams' federal business trended recently?
sections.body: Softrams' obligations have grown each reported year from FY21 through FY26. Fiscal-year totals were $70.2M in FY21, $77.7M in FY22, $125M in FY23, $158M in FY24, $207M in FY25, and $217M in FY26. Year-over-year obligations are up 4.8% in the current fiscal-year-to-date period. The award profile shows 18 awards so far in FY2026 with an average award size of $12M.

faq.q: How much does Softrams make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Softrams has $217M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Softrams' fiscal-year obligations increased steadily from $70.2M in FY21 to $217M in FY26, and Softrams shows 18 awards this year with an average award size of $12M.

The Department of Health and Human Services buys the most from Softrams, obligating $177M in FY2026 to date. The Department of Veterans Affairs obligated $25.9M and the Department of Homeland Security obligated $13.4M; smaller obligations include $279K with the General Services Administration and separate entries list the Department of Defense and the Department of Labor without dollar figures shown here.

faq.q: What does Softrams sell to the government?
faq.a: Softrams sells largely IT and systems services to the government, with Custom Computer Programming Services at $182M and Computer Systems Design Services at $34.8M in FY2026 to date. Softrams also records other work across its reported NAICS categories.

faq.q: Which Softrams contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Contract expiration dates and a list of specific expiring contracts are not provided in these figures, so contract expirations cannot be determined from the available data. The dataset shows current obligations and markets but does not list expiring-contract dates or award-value expirations.
